newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KOREA FIRST SHARES OPEN LIMIT UP.
newsitem.headline: KOREA FIRST SHARES OPEN LIMIT UP.

text.p: Shares of Korea First Bank opened at their upper daily limit on Thursday as investors bought shares on hopes of government help, brokers said.
Korea First Bank opened up 270 won to 3,760.
It was also the most heavily traded stock with 154,310 shares changing hands, 10 minutes after the market opened.
"Investors are buying Korea First Bank stocks on expectations of government help including special loans," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The finance ministry said on Wednesday it was mulling ways to help Korea First Bank which has been hit by loan defaults by big conglomerates.
Possible government steps included special loans from the central bank, rights issue offerings or lower provisions for non-performing loans. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5643
